newsitem.title: FRANCE: Unoccupied house destroyed by Corsican bomb.
newsitem.headline: Unoccupied house destroyed by Corsican bomb.

text.p: A powerful bomb early on Friday wrecked an unoccupied summer holiday home near the Corsican resort of Propriano , police said.

The words "FLNC - Historical Wing" -- a main separatist group on this French Mediterranean island -- were found daubed on the outside walls of the house, which is owned by a woman who lives in mainland France.
Police gave no details but separatist groups, and, or local criminals, are known to carry out such attacks against owners of holiday homes who refuse to pay "protection money" for their property.
The attack came a day after police arrested six people in connection with a weekend blitz of bombings by separatist guerrillas but released them without charge after a few hours.

Police said that among those held in Bastia and Ghisonaccia on the French Mediterranean island were employees of a security firm owned by a leader of Cuncolta Naziunalista, the legal wing of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC).
The FLNC exploded 76 small devices in Corsica on Sunday in a show of strength in response to a police crackdown in recent weeks. Three of the Cuncolta's main political leaders are in detention.

No one was injured in Sunday's coordinated pre-dawn blitz of small blasts. Damage was mostly limited to smashed windows or damaged doorways at post offices, tax offices and other symbols of French state authority in towns and villages
